designStatus: Original untested source-fit protocols; no learner observations or private state changes

protocols.requiredTask: Actually hold, transport and serve a suitable ordinary food/drink quantity with a cup/container/spoon as the position requires; vary the object and inspect grip, stability, tipping and spill control.
protocols.reuseCheck: The snack claim includes serving, but a child can prepare a wrap successfully without demonstrating pouring or spoon control. Do not infer every functional manipulation from snack preparation.
protocols.boundary: Actual glass/spoon/serving/pouring duties remain resource-specific practical checks over the serving component, not new per-container states or claims of whole snack mastery.

protocols.requiredTask: Produce actual spontaneous/controlled marks with the relevant crayon/brush/wrist/hand action; observe comfortable tool control rather than impose recognisable pictures on a spontaneous-mark position.
protocols.mismatch: The existing whole WB claim also requires all 26 lowercase English letters and consistent lined-paper size, so generic motor grip does not establish its whole claim or named-language inventory.
protocols.decision: Use one approved shared mark-making operation; keep thumb/finger handling, spontaneous production and varied material exploration explicit and separate from named-language WB requirements.

protocols.requiredTask: Perform actual clay/card folding/rolling/shaping or marked-line cutting for the source case, and retain the full Ft card/fabric, joining, safety and storage checks.
protocols.reuseReason: Material change alone does not establish a separate mastery claim; actual manipulation and precision still need a task.

protocols.requiredTask: Use a varied actual manipulation panel with threading/placement/fastening/cutting/joining/pouring actions from the source case, respecting which items are illustrative. Record independent two-hand coordination where required.
protocols.reuseReason: Craft, serving and threading contributions are direct only for their actual operations. Naming a motor action or completing one convenient item does not close every source requirement.
protocols.wholeClaimBoundary: Complete unchanged craft, serving and safe hand-sewing tasks are assessed independently. The actual button/zip/placement/pouring panel remains necessary; no single convenient component silently establishes the others.

protocols.requiredTask: Build a stable small-block structure/tower and copy a supplied block/shape arrangement; retain full QNx composition/description/matching-halves and 2VR build/draw checks as applicable.
protocols.scopeBoundary: Two-hand independent building is observed directly in the declared task, not inferred from a geometric explanation or used to impose a universal body norm.

protocols.requiredTask: Actually complete a source-fit 10–25-piece arrangement puzzle using shapes and a suitable whole outline; transfer to a changed whole. Retain the complete Mqq shape-composition/recomposition checks.
protocols.reuseReason: Mqq already has an actual fitting-pieces puzzle assessment. Piece count is a source performance condition, not an additional maths difficulty-level topic. Do not claim arbitrary picture-jigsaw knowledge from one geometric puzzle.

protocols.requiredTask: Use the source-permitted numeric-production route with complete unchanged oAK 0–9 formation and legibility checks. Record the actual numeral material set; this does not infer mastery of every script or of English letters.
protocols.reuseReason: The source permits letters or numbers, and oAK has no hard English-alphabet prerequisite; WB is only a soft support.

protocols.requiredTask: Observe the child’s comfortable self-selected hand use over drawing/writing tasks. Do not force right/left dominance, equate switching with lack of knowledge, or infer a stable trait from one event.
protocols.recommendedRepresentation: Retained in-scope contextual motor-development observation with an actual task protocol, not a new binary dominant-hand mastery topic or learner score. Other fine-motor production requirements remain separate.

protocols.requiredTask: Actually use a stringing board or string whole flowers as the selected source case; beads alone do not meet this position. Separately test the complete Ff claim with a suitable supervised primary fabric-sewing task: thread a needle, secure the start, make a running-stitch seam, secure the finish and check it holds.
protocols.reuseCheck: Beading alone does not establish sewing. Existing 9–12 guidance is not a distinct mastery claim, but an IN 6–8 association requires a justified age-appropriate whole sewing task; no simplified younger sewing clone or age lowering from one bead example.
protocols.wholePrimaryTask: Use a suitable supervised actual fabric running join, threading the needle, securing start/end, storing it safely and checking the seam. Existing 9–12 contexts remain alongside this primary 6–8 source-fit task.
